Morning Glory Pool in the Upper Geyser Basin was another heavily affected thermal feature.

Long before Yellowstone National Park became known for strict rules around its hot springs and geysers, visitors were encouraged to marvel at some of the park’s unusual thermal features.One of them was Handkerchief Pool, a small spring in the Black Sand Basin. According to National Park Service, visitors could put a handkerchief into it and watch it disappear into the water. The item would then come back to the surface after being moved through the pool’s water currents. Vistors believed the items came back scrubed and clean.But visitors did not limit themselves to handkerchiefs. Over time, people began putting other objects into the pool. This gradually turned a natural thermal feature into a collection point for rubbish and other items and started to interfere with the pool’s natural activity.Handkerchief Pool’s activity eventually stopped in 1926. According to Yellowstone Science, a log was shoved into the pool’s vent, blocking the feature and stopping the movement of water that produced its unusual effect. Visitors, however, continued to throw objects into the pool even after it stopped working properly.The problem was not limited to the log. The pool had accumulated a large amount of material over the years. Objects that visitors had thrown into the water remained inside the feature, adding to the blockage and making it harder for the pool to function normally.Also, the park contains geothermal systems that depend on underground water movement, heat and narrow openings. Blocking those openings with foreign material can change or stop the natural activity of a spring. The damage was eventually investigated and a major cleanup was carried out in 1929.When Ranger Carlos Davis cleaned the pool in 1929, the amount and variety of material removed was astounding. More than one and a half bushels of debris were taken out of the spring.The debris included coins, more than 100 hairpins, nails, bolts, a horseshoe, a broken bottle, part of a spark plug, badges, nuts and about a dozen handkerchiefs.The 1929 cleanup helped improve the convection currents in the pool, but the work did not completely solve the problem. Records indicated that further work would be needed.Other springs and geysers were also affected when visitors threw rocks, coins, bottles and other objects into them. Minute Geyser in Norris Geyser Basin was among the most vandalised. It once erupted about once a minute, sometimes reaching 40 feet, but rocks and other material were repeatedly thrown into its vent. By 1969, the vent was clogged with rocks cemented together by mineral-rich spring water, causing the geyser’s activity to shift to a side vent. Its eruptions then became irregular and reached only a few feet.Morning Glory Pool in the Upper Geyser Basin was another heavily affected thermal feature. Before the road near it was diverted in 1971, visitors threw coins, rocks, logs, bottles and clothing into the spring. Repeated cleanups removed some of the material, but continued additions clogged the vent. The pool’s temperature may have fallen, allowing algae to grow, although Yellowstone geologists noted that natural causes may also have contributed to the change.The story of Handkerchief Pool did not end with the 1929 cleanup. In 1950, park geologist George Marler cleaned the spring again, removing the log and gravel that had washed into it. Water flowed into the pool once more, but the feature had been permanently changed by its long period of inactivity, with algae mats spreading onto its rims.Geysers and hot springs are relatively rare geological features and can be vulnerable to human activity. Many geysers around the world have been altered or lost because of geothermal energy development and tourism. Yellowstone was protected as the world’s first national park largely because of its geyser basins.
Article Summary: Handkerchief Pool was a visitor favourite for its ability to pull in handkerchiefs and return them washed and clean. Over time, people began putting other objects into the pool. This gradually turned a natural thermal feature into a collection point for rubbish and other items.

Article Title: Artemis II astronauts are set to receive America's highest spaceflight honour on August 28
Article Text:
Artemis II crew NASA astronauts in the White House Oval Office with President Donald J Trump, PC: White House/NASA

Why Artemis II was such a significant mission

Why so few astronauts have received the Congressional Space Medal of Honour

What Artemis II proved for NASA's return to the Moon

The four astronauts who flew NASA 's Artemis II mission around the Moon are set to receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor, one of the highest distinctions the United States awards for achievements in human spaceflight. According to NASA, President Donald J. Trump will present the medal to NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, during a ceremony at 11 a.m. EDT on Friday, August 28, at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston. The honour comes after the crew completed a roughly 10-day mission that launched in April 2026 and carried them around the Moon before returning safely to Earth. Artemis II marked the first crewed mission to travel beyond low Earth orbit since the Apollo era and sent humans farther from Earth than any previous crewed mission, making it a major milestone in NASA's return to deep-space exploration.Artemis II was the first crewed flight of NASA's Orion spacecraft and the first crewed mission in more than 50 years to travel beyond low Earth orbit. Wiseman served as commander, Glover as pilot, while Koch and Hansen served as mission specialists.The crew travelled around the Moon before returning to Earth, putting Orion's life-support systems, navigation, communications and other technologies through their first major crewed test in deep space. Hansen's participation also gave the mission an international significance. He became the first Canadian to travel to the Moon and the first non-American astronaut to fly on a mission to the lunar region. The mission concluded with the crew's splashdown on April 10, 2026, after roughly 10 days in space.The Congressional Space Medal of Honour is awarded to astronauts whose achievements have made an exceptional contribution to the welfare of the nation and humanity. It is separate from NASA's own Distinguished Service Medal and is among the rarest major American honours specifically associated with human spaceflight. According to CBS News, only 30 astronauts had received the Congressional Space Medal of Honour before the Artemis II crew were selected as recipients. Previous honourees include some of the most famous names in American space exploration, including Neil Armstrong and John Glenn. The medal's rarity reflects the standard required for receiving it. It is not simply an award for completing a successful mission, but recognition reserved for extraordinary achievements and contributions to space exploration. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is also expected to attend the August 28 ceremony alongside Trump and the Artemis II astronauts.Artemis II was designed as a test of the systems and procedures NASA will need for later crewed lunar missions. Unlike Artemis I, which sent an uncrewed Orion spacecraft around the Moon in 2022, Artemis II carried people into deep space for the first time under the Artemis program The mission therefore provided NASA with experience operating a crewed spacecraft far beyond low Earth orbit, while also allowing astronauts to evaluate conditions that cannot be fully reproduced on Earth. The flight is part of NASA's wider Artemis program, which aims to return astronauts to the lunar surface and establish a longer-term human presence around and on the Moon. NASA also views the lunar program as preparation for eventual human missions to Mars. For the Artemis II crew, the August 28 ceremony will mark the formal recognition of a mission that reopened a chapter in human exploration that had been closed since the final Apollo flights more than half a century ago.
Article Summary: President Donald J. Trump will present the medal to NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen. The honour comes after the crew completed a roughly 10-day mission that launched in April 2026 and carried them around the Moon before returning safely to Earth. Artemis II marked the first crewed mission to travel beyond low Earth orbit since the Apollo era and sent humans farther from Earth than any previous mission.

Article Title: 15 newborns killed in fire at Islamabad hospital's gynaecology ward in Pakistan
Article Text:
The fire reportedly started after an air-conditioner compressor exploded inside the nursery, according to rescue sources.

Poll Vote & Share your view What should hospitals prioritise to prevent fire-related tragedies? Stronger fire-safety measures Regular safety inspections 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

15 newborns died after a fire broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad on Wednesday.According to PIMS officials, the nursery housed 16 newborns when the fire broke out, with only one baby rescued from the ward, reported local outlet Geo News. The fire reportedly started after an air-conditioner compressor exploded inside the nursery, according to rescue officials.The blaze broke out at around 7 am in the gynaecology ward of the hospital on the third floor of the MCH ward, in Pakistan's federal capital. Rescue teams were deployed to the hospital and worked to extinguish the fire and evacuate those inside while carrying out cooling operations at the site.According to the district administration, 14 of the 15 children killed were completely burnt.The incident has raised concerns over safety measures in the hospital's neonatal and maternity facilities.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an immediate investigation into the incident and directed authorities to identify those responsible and take strict action. He expressed deep grief over the deaths, saying that a tragedy involving children was an “irreparable loss”, and said he shared the grief of the bereaved parents.The Prime Minister also directed authorities to conduct a detailed review of fire-safety arrangements and the factors that contributed to the incident, with the aim of preventing similar tragedies in hospitals.Meanwhile, an inquiry committee headed by the additional deputy commissioner general has also been formed to determine how the fire started and establish responsibility. The blaze broke out in the hospital’s gynaecology ward, where the nursery was located.
Article Summary: 15 newborns died after a fire broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences in Islamabad. The fire reportedly started after an air-conditioner compressor exploded inside the nursery, according to rescue sources. Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an immediate investigation into the incident.

Article Title: Five labourers gunned down at construction site in Pakistan's Balochistan
Article Text: Five labourers from Pakistan’s Punjab province were shot dead at a construction site in Balochistan’s Pishin district, a provincial government official said Tuesday, according to news agency PTI.The labourers were killed by unidentified gunmen in Saranan town on Monday morning, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said. Their bodies were sent to their hometowns in Punjab for burial.Arrangements were made to transport the bodies to their respective villages in Ahmedpur Sharqia and Bahawalpur, Rind said. Security forces have launched a search operation to track down the attackers.Balochistan chief minister Sarfaraz Bugti condemned the killings and vowed action against those responsible."Those shedding the blood of innocent laborers deserve no leniency," Bugti said in a statement issued by his office. "The cowardly acts of terrorists cannot weaken the provincial government's resolve."Saranan town has witnessed militant attacks since last week. A few days ago, gunmen attacked a police station in the town and fled with weapons, ammunition and two vehicles.Banned Baloch insurgent groups have frequently targeted workers and labourers from other provinces working in Balochistan.In July, five barbers from Multan were shot dead in Mashkail town after armed men on motorcycles opened fire at their barber shop.Last month, six labourers from Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were abducted in the Nasirabad area of Turbat district. Their bullet-riddled bodies were later found in a remote area, police said.Security and law enforcement agencies have been conducting a large-scale operation against insurgent groups in parts of Balochistan since early July. However, the attacks have continued.In a separate incident on Sunday, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil of Mohmand district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.Police retaliated with gunfire, forcing the attackers to flee. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger. An investigation is underway.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which borders Afghanistan, has witnessed recurring militant violence, including attacks linked to insurgent groups, cross-border movement of fighters and repeated military operations.
Article Summary: The labourers were killed by unidentified gunmen in Saranan town on Monday morning. Security forces have launched a search operation to track down the attackers. Baloch insurgent groups have frequently targeted workers and labourers from other provinces working in Balochistan. In July, five barbers from Multan were shot dead in Mashkail town.

Article Title: Pakistan army officer pulls gun, fires in air amid student protest at Peshawar university- video
Article Text:
Sarhad University, Peshawar, Pakistan (Picture from X)

A Pakistan army officer opened fire into the air during a student protest at Sarhad University in Peshawar, triggering chaos and a scuffle on the campus, according to local media reports and videos circulating online.The incident comes amid growing unrest in Pakistan, with protests and demonstrations also being reported from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Balochistan, adding to the challenges facing the country's military and political establishment.According to reports, the officer, said to be a colonel, was the husband of a faculty member at Sarhad University. He reportedly got into a heated confrontation with protesting students, which soon escalated into a physical scuffle.Videos shared by several social media accounts purportedly show the officer striking students with a stick amid the confrontation. As tensions escalated, he allegedly pulled out a pistol and initially pointed it towards the protesters before raising the weapon in the air.The officer was then seen firing shots into the air, sparking panic and further uproar on the university campus.Reports said the officer has been taken into custody, while the Pakistan army has ordered an inquiry into the incident.
Article Summary: Pakistan army officer opened fire during student protest at Sarhad University. Incident triggered chaos and a scuffle on the campus, according to reports. Incident comes amid growing unrest in Pakistan, with protests and demonstrations also being reported from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Balochistan.

Article Title: ‘CTA intentionally prevented’: PTI alleges negligence over Imran Khan’s hospital visit
Article Text:
Imran Khan’s medical care under scrutiny

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the inquiry committee established by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will lead to accountability? Yes, it will No, it won't 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, on Monday criticised what it called the “continued failure” of authorities at a state-run hospital, alleging that a CT Coronary Angiography (CTA) scheduled for Khan was not conducted despite cardiologists warning of potential cardiac complications.In a statement on Sunday, PTI central secretary Information Sheikh Waqas Akram said authorities had failed to provide the 73-year-old Khan with the medically recommended diagnostic test despite a functional CT scanner being available at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), Dawn reported."This cannot be dismissed as an isolated administrative lapse; it reflects a deeply troubling pattern,” Akram said.Akram also cited a Supreme Court order directing Khan to undergo a comprehensive medical examination and treatment at Shifa International Hospital.He alleged that authorities had bypassed the directive and instead transferred Khan to a facility where the CT angiography was not conducted.“When the necessary facilities were available at Shifa International, deliberately taking Khan to a hospital unable or unwilling to perform the procedure raises a grave question: was the decision made in advance to prevent the CT Coronary Angiography from being conducted?” he asked."Even the government’s own doctors considered this diagnostic test necessary,” Akram added.Akram said a government medical board examined Khan on August 10 after he complained of heart palpitations and severe headaches.He said a cardiologist at PIMS had recommended a CTA on August 1 after Khan experienced fluctuating blood pressure and restlessness, citing potential cardiac complications given his age and prolonged isolation.Taking note of the reports, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday formed an inquiry committee, headed by the Establishment Division secretary, to establish the facts and determine responsibility.Commenting on the Prime Minister’s decision to constitute an inquiry committee following reports that Imran Khan’s CTA was not conducted, Akram said the move raised “serious questions as to why the medically recommended test was not conducted in the first instance. Why coordination between the cardiology and radiology departments had failed, and why Imran Khan was not taken to Shifa International despite the availability of the required facilities there”."Imran Khan’s heart health cannot be subjected to political calculations, administrative excuses or further delay,” Akram said."Political victimisation must never be permitted to endanger a human life through the denial or postponement of essential medical care. The decision to take him to a facility where the required test was not conducted, despite the availability of the necessary facilities at Shifa International, has created serious concerns that the procedure was intentionally prevented,” he alleged."The government and all relevant authorities will bear full responsibility for any further deterioration in his condition,” Akram added.Meanwhile, former India captains Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar are among 21 former international cricket captains who have written to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging authorities to ensure proper medical treatment and the welfare of Imran Khan.The letter, initiated by former Australia captain Greg Chappell, marks the second appeal by former international cricketers calling for humane treatment and adequate medical care for the 73-year-old Khan.Khan was arrested on August 5, 2023, in connection with a corruption case and has remained in custody since then. He is currently lodged in Adiala Jail, a detention facility on the outskirts of Rawalpindi.Khan’s relatives and supporters have repeatedly alleged human rights violations and accused authorities of restricting his access to adequate medical care, family visits and legal counsel.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, on Monday criticised what it called the “continued failure” of authorities at a state-run hospital. PTI alleges that a CT Coronary Angiography (CTA) scheduled for Khan was not conducted despite cardiologists warning of potential cardiac complications. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday formed an inquiry committee, headed by the Establishment Division secretary.

Article Title: ‘You are powerful, but remember 1971?’ Pakistani politician takes fresh swipe at Army
Article Text:
Fazlur Rehman (File photo)

(With ANI inputs)

Pakistani politician and Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman continued his verbal attacks on the Pakistan Army, recalling the military's decisive defeat in the 1971 war with India that led to the creation of Bangladesh, then known as East Pakistan.“‘We are the protectors of this country. No one’s father can harm this country.’ I agree, you are very powerful,” Rehman remarked at a JUI (F) convention in Peshawar, targeting Pakistan’s top military leadership.He recalled how the Pakistan Army laid down its arms in 1971, just a day after then-President and military ruler General Yahya Khan declared that it would fight until the end."But I remember, and maybe there are some elders who remember, that in December 1971, one day before laying down arms, General Yahya Khan addressed the army and said, we will fight in the streets, in the deserts, in the fields, in the factories, in the mountains, and we will fight against them. We will fight. We heard these big words then," Rehman added.The JUI-F further chief questioned why the public is being subjected to "severe hardships" while the establishment remains "insensitive" to their misery.“Why are you putting the country and the people to the test? Why are you having fun when your public is suffering? And today is 2026. When the revolution came in Afghanistan in 1989, and the war started, now you tell me, it’s been 45-46 years, blood has been flowing on the same line for about half a century.When blood flows like this, then it is a sign of geographical changes,” Rehman remarked.Warning that persistent state oppression and ongoing conflict threaten the nation’s integrity and could signal territorial disintegration, he stated, “It is a sign of oppression. Then at least inform us of your intentions. We are tolerating it and will continue to tolerate it. It will continue. A few more days, my dear, just a few more days. We are forced to take a breath in the shade of oppression. If we endure the oppression for a little longer, if we suffer, if we cry, it is the legacy of our ancestors. We are helpless.”Rehman’s remarks came days after he challenged the military to enter politics directly, declaring, “If you want to do politics, then take off the uniform and come; participate in the elections, and it will become clear what votes people give to those in uniform. It is your prerogative to give government to whomever you want, and to snatch it away from whomever you wish.”
Article Summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman continued his verbal attacks on the Pakistan Army. He recalled the military's decisive defeat in the 1971 war with India that led to the creation of Bangladesh. He questioned why the public is being subjected to "severe hardships" while the establishment remains "insensitive"

Article Title: Pakistan: Security official killed by unidentified gunmen; 5 cops injured in separate grenade blast
Article Text:
According to police, two unidentified armed men targeted the security official. (Photo credit: IANS)

Five policemen injured in grenade attack

A security official was killed on Sunday after unidentified gunmen opened fire in northwest Pakistan, police said, according to news agency PTI.The incident took place within the jurisdiction of Badaber Police Station on the outskirts of Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.According to police, two unidentified armed men riding a motorcycle targeted the official, who was posted with the Counter Terrorism Department.He was killed on the spot, while the assailants fled the scene following the attack. Police cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to trace the attackers.No individual or group has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.In a separate incident in Mohmand district, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil, police said.Police retaliated with gunfire, forcing the attackers to flee. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger. An investigation is underway.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which borders Afghanistan, has witnessed recurring militant violence, cross-border movement of fighters and military operations.Pakistan's federal government has blamed the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) for attacks in areas bordering Afghanistan since a ceasefire agreement between the two sides ended in November 2022.
Article Summary: A security official was killed on Sunday after unidentified gunmen opened fire in northwest Pakistan. In a separate incident, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger.

Article Title: Pakistan power crisis: Karachi residents riot amid outages lasting hours, block major roads
Article Text:
Protesters blocked major roads and intersections, burned tyres and clashed with K-Electric personnel over prolonged blackouts (ANI photo)

Power protests erupted across several parts of Karachi as residents took to the streets over prolonged and unannounced outages, blocking major roads and burning tyres while demanding restoration of electricity.Demonstrations were reported in Pak Colony, Liaquatabad, Gharibabad, Nishtar Road, Bhimpura and Ranchore Line, disrupting traffic across key parts of Pakistan’s commercial capital. In Liaquatabad, protesters blocked major intersections, while clashes between traders and K-Electric (KE) staff over outages escalated into tyre-burning on Nishtar Road, as reported by local news outle Dawn.Residents said they were facing 12 hours or more of daily power cuts, often without adequate notice. The outages have also disrupted water supplies as pumping stations remain shut when electricity is unavailable, adding to public anger.“Bill-paying citizens are being punished with 12-hour load-shedding,” a protester in Liaquatabad said.The crisis also hit businesses and households, with residents reporting spoiled food, disrupted studies and sleepless nights as fans remained unusable during blackouts.The protests compounded an already severe traffic situation in the city. Roads were also closed for traditional Chup Tazia processions, while the power protests triggered additional blockades. Traffic police diverted vehicles to alternative routes, but those too became congested.Asif Khan, a private-sector employee, told Dawn he took four hours to travel from SITE to Liaquatabad after leaving work around 5pm. Another commuter said an ambulance carrying his feverish mother was stuck for about two hours near Civic Centre while they were travelling to a doctor in Saddar.“We pay bills on time but still face 12-hour power outages. Today we couldn’t even reach home,” commuter Imran from Gharibabad said.KE, however, attributed the prolonged outages in some affected areas to electricity theft and unpaid bills. A company spokesperson said outstanding dues from defaulters in Bandhani Colony and Rexer Line had crossed PKR 3 billion, adding that the duration of load-shedding depended on “electricity theft and the level of losses in the area”.The protests come as Karachi continues to grapple with an electricity crisis that is also affecting water supply, businesses and daily life across densely populated neighbourhoods.
Article Summary: Demonstrations reported in Pak Colony, Liaquatabad, Gharibabad, Nishtar Road, Bhimpura and Ranchore Line. Protesters blocked major roads and intersections, burned tyres and clashed with K-Electric personnel. Residents said they were facing 12 hours or more of daily power cuts, often without adequate notice.

Article Title: 'India could use water as weapon': Pakistan minister as Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance
Article Text:
Pakistan minister Ahsan Iqbal (File photo)

Pakistan minister Ahsan Iqbal has said India could “weaponise” the Indus Water Treaty (IWT) and expressed hope that “better sense” would prevail to prevent the two neighbours from going to war again, this time over water.He noted that the treaty had remained “untouchable” for almost seven decades since it was signed in 1960, but New Delhi has now been kept in abeyance “unilaterally."“...Indus Water Treaty that has stood the test of time for the last 70 years. India and Pakistan fought several wars, but it (IWT) was considered untouchable because it is an international agreement, and this time around the Indian government has unilaterally held it in abeyance... first time probably water has been weaponised in history,” Iqbal told the Asia Society.“We (Pakistan) now face this threat that they (India) can use water as a weapon to deny Pakistan when it needs it for its crops and release it when we don't need it... We are using all the diplomatic means to make sure that we don't have future wars on water because we have already seen lots of wars,” the minister added.He further stated that South Asian countries should instead focus on issues such as development, poverty, illiteracy and the youth “bulge”, describing the region as the “least integrated” in the world."So we hope that there is better sense in our neighbour's (India) mind and we don't see that water is weaponised and we go to another conflict with India over water because Pakistan cannot surrender at any cost the future of its 250 million people for its food security and right of water. If we let it happen, then every state that is on the lower side of water supply would be hostage to any country that controls the rivers," the Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) leader remarked.Iqbal's remarks came days after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif warned India of a “direct response” for putting the IWT in abeyance.“India proved itself an enemy of peace by unilaterally and illegally suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. I declare in clear terms that every single drop of Pakistan's water is our red line. If India does not come to its senses, it will be responded to directly,” Sharif said on August 13, on the eve of Pakistan's Independence Day.New Delhi put the agreement in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year. Since then, Pakistani leaders have repeatedly called water their “red line” and threatened India over the move, describing it as an “act of war.”
Article Summary: Ahsan Iqbal says India could use water as a weapon to deny Pakistan when it needs it for its crops. New Delhi put the agreement in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year. Pakistani leaders have repeatedly called water their “red line” and threatened India.

Article Title: ‘In contempt for gathering people’: Pak blames ex PM Imran Khan’s party for hospital transfer
Article Text:
Pakistan government statement on Imran Khan's hospital transfer

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you view the involvement of PTI workers during Imran Khan transfer to the hospital? Justified, they were supporting their leader Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Govt says court order was followed

NEW DELHI: The Pakistan government on Saturday blamed jailed former prime minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party for his transfer to a state-run hospital instead of the private facility ordered by the Supreme Court for his medical checkup.Information minister Attaullah Tarar said the government was forced to take 73-year-old Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) after a large number of PTI workers gathered outside Shifa International Hospital.The development came after Khan’s sister, Uzma Khan, approached the Supreme Court alleging that the government and senior officials had violated its order to shift the former prime minister to the private hospital.The Supreme Court had on August 18 directed authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa Hospital within two days and keep him there until the next hearing on September 16. Instead, Khan was taken to PIMS and later returned to jail after doctors declared him fit.Tarar alleged that PTI workers gathered along the route to Shifa Hospital, removed barriers and created social media content, leaving authorities with no option but to shift Khan elsewhere.“Contempt has definitely happened,” Tarar said, accusing Khan’s sister and PTI of violating the court’s directions by turning the medical checkup into a political issue.The minister maintained that the government had implemented the Supreme Court’s order “in letter and spirit”. He said the medical examination was conducted transparently, Khan’s sister was present and doctors from Shifa Hospital were involved in the process.The Supreme Court’s order followed months of concerns raised by Khan’s family and supporters over his health, particularly an eye condition diagnosed earlier this year. Khan was taken to PIMS several times after being diagnosed with right central retinal vein occlusion in late January.A report submitted by jail authorities to the Supreme Court said his eye condition had improved significantly and that his vision was “almost normal”.Khan has been lodged in Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail since 2023 in connection with several cases.
Article Summary: Pakistan government blames jailed former prime minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party for his transfer to a state-run hospital. Information minister Attaullah Tarar said the government was forced to take 73-year-old Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences. Tarar alleged that PTI workers gathered along the route to Shifa Hospital, removed barriers and created social media content.

Article Title: Big crisis brewing in Rawalpindi? Pakistan deploys army for ‘sensitive duties’
Article Text:
The decision comes days after a man allegedly linked to former prime minister Imran Khan's party.

Army deployment follows security incident

Rawalpindi has strategic importance

The Pakistan government has authorised the deployment of the army in Rawalpindi for six months following a request from the Punjab home department for what it described as "sensitive security duties".The decision allows three companies of the Pakistan Army to be deployed in the city under Article 245 of the Pakistani Constitution, which permits the armed forces to assist the civil administration in maintaining security."The federal government, exercising the powers conferred under Article 245 of the Constitution of Pakistan, is pleased to authorise the deployment of three companies of the Pakistan Army for sensitive security duties in Rawalpindi," according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control on Friday.The notification said the deployment was intended to prevent a potential security problem and ensure that authorities could respond quickly if an unexpected situation arose.It said that the decision was taken "to avoid any undesirable situation as well as to respond effectively in any unforeseen situation as per the requirement of the district administration".The decision comes days after a man allegedly linked to former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party opened fire at security forces in Rawalpindi.He was subsequently killed in retaliatory firing.State-run PTV News, citing security sources, reported that the attacker was a resident of Khyber district and an "active PTI member". According to the report, a PTI flag, bullets and weapons were recovered from him.The PTI, however, rejected any connection with the incident. The party said it had nothing to do with terrorism and accused authorities of attempting to associate the party with the attack.The deployment is particularly significant because Rawalpindi is home to the Pakistan Army's General Headquarters, the military's top command centre.The city is therefore an important military and administrative centre, and the decision to deploy army personnel there comes amid heightened security concerns following the recent shooting incident.The deployment has been authorised for six months, with the troops to perform duties requested by the district administration under the constitutional provision allowing the military to assist civilian authorities.
Article Summary: Three companies of the Pakistan Army will be deployed in Rawalpindi for six months. The decision comes after a man allegedly linked to Imran Khan's party opened fire in the city. The deployment is intended to prevent a potential security problem and ensure that authorities can respond quickly.

Article Title: 'Repeatedly tortured': Imran Khan's sister alleges abuse in jail as ex-Pakistan PM returns to prison
Article Text:
‘He was repeatedly tortured in jail’: Imran Khan's sister alleges mistreatment

PTI files contempt petition

Supporters gather after brief hospital visit

Pakistan's jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan repeatedly told his sister that he was being tortured in prison, she said on Saturday, a day after he was taken to a state-run hospital for a brief medical examination and sent back to jail.Khan's sister, Uzma Khan, attended his examination at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad and said the former prime minister was physically fit but had repeatedly complained of torture.“Khan told me that he is being repeatedly tortured in prison”, she told the media.The interior and law ministries, along with jail authorities, have not responded to a Reuters request for comment on the allegation.Khan was taken to PIMS overnight on Friday after the Supreme Court had directed authorities to transfer him from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for a medical examination. He was declared medically fit and returned to prison within hours.Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party on Saturday filed a contempt petition against the government, accusing authorities of violating the Supreme Court's order by taking him to PIMS instead of the private hospital named by the court.The petition seeks action against senior government officials and asks that Khan be taken to Shifa International Hospital for treatment, PTI legal adviser Naeem Panjutha said."The petition seeks action against the ​prime minister, law minister, information minister" and other government officials, Panjutha said, adding that it also calls for Khan's treatment at the private hospital ordered by the court.The PTI also alleged that Khan was denied access to his personal physician, which it said amounted to another breach of the Supreme Court's directive.A three-judge Supreme Court bench had on Tuesday directed authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital within two days for a medical examination.The PTI interprets the order as requiring Khan to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September.Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the decision to take Khan to PIMS instead of the court-named private hospital was made because of security concerns.Khan declared medically fit, sent back to jailKhan was examined by a team of doctors, including an ophthalmologist, cardiologist and physician, before being declared medically fit and sent back to Adiala jail in Rawalpindi."A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist and a physician conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit," Tarar said.Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and maintains that the cases against him are politically motivated. The government denies the allegation.His lawyers have previously said his health has deteriorated in prison and that he has suffered substantial loss of vision in his right eye. The government has maintained that medical reports have found no condition requiring immediate treatment.Khan's supporters gathered along roads in Islamabad overnight, throwing flowers at a vehicle believed to be carrying him to the hospital.The scenes were broadcast live on Pakistani television, in a notable departure from recent years when broadcasters often avoided mentioning Khan's name.PTI leaders have warned that the latest developments could increase pressure on the government and fuel fresh demonstrations."After what happened yesterday, the pressure (on authorities) will double," Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said, adding that preparations for a protest march planned for September 27 had picked up.Khan's arrest and imprisonment have remained a major source of political tension in Pakistan. His arrest in 2023 triggered widespread protests, including attacks on military installations, and his supporters continue to demand his release.
Article Summary: Imran Khan repeatedly told his sister that he was being tortured in prison, she says. Khan was taken to a state-run hospital for a brief medical examination and sent back to jail. He was declared medically fit and returned to prison within hours. Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and maintains that the cases against him are politically motivated.

Article Title: Imran Khan's kin say Pak govt violated court order for not taking ex-PM to private hospital
Article Text:
Imran Khan shifted back to jail after medical examination

Family alleges violation of court order

NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan was shifted back to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi early Friday, hours after he was taken for a medical examination amid a legal battle over his health and demands from his family and supporters for better medical care.Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, Pakistan's information minister Attaullah Tarar said, news agaency PTI reports. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am.The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital following a medical report that said he was suffering from “level three plus” anxiety.Khan's family has repeatedly raised concerns about his access to adequate medical treatment while in custody. His sister, Uzma Khan, was present during the medical examination at PIMS, according to AP. They have accused authorities of violating a court order by taking him to a government hospital for a medical examination instead of a private hospital designated by the court.She alleged that during their meeting, Khan complained of being kept in solitary confinement, which she described as “mental torture” for the former prime minister.Khan’s personal physician, Faisal Sultan, said he had been taken to Shifa International Hospital, where he waited for Khan until early Friday. He was later informed that Khan had instead been returned to Adiala prison in Rawalpindi.Tarar said authorities changed the plan because of security concerns after supporters of Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) gathered outside Shifa International Hospital or were heading there.Khan has been in custody since his arrest on August 5, 2023, in a corruption case.
Article Summary: Imran Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am. The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital.

Article Title: Ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan returns to Adiala Jail after medical examination at Islamabad hospital
Article Text:
73-year-old cricket legend facing health issues after 3 years of imprisonment

Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan on Friday returned to Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail shortly after undergoing a medical examination at Shifa Hospital in Islamabad.The development was confirmed to Reuters by a member of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.The 73-year-old cricket legend has been facing health issues after spending more than three years in prison following his tenure as prime minister.Khan was taken to Shifa Hospital days after the Supreme Court ordered a medical examination. An official from the Shehbaz Sharif-led government said Islamabad was complying with the Supreme Court's order to facilitate his medical examination.Khan's party and family had sought permission for him to remain in hospital.A three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination amid prolonged concerns raised by his family and personal doctors over his health and access to treatment.The court directed that a medical board, including specialists and his personal physician, Faisal Sultan, examine him.The Supreme Court's order came after former Pakistan president Arif Alvi shared Khan's vitals and raised concerns over what he described as "alarming" medical reports.In a post on X, Alvi said, "Imran Khan's medical reports are alarming. I have gone through them with several specialists, and I am writing this in plain language so every Pakistani can understand exactly what is happening."Alvi also highlighted Khan's health concerns, citing his "anxiety and stress levels", "palpitations," and "high blood pressure." He added that while sleeplessness was not mentioned in the report, Khan's medication appeared to suggest the problem.
Article Summary: Imran Khan returned to Adiala Jail after medical examination at Shifa Hospital in Islamabad. Khan, 73, has been facing health issues after spending more than three years in prison following his tenure as prime minister. A three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination.

Article Title: Ex-Pak PM Imran Khan moved to private hospital from prison after SC order
Article Text:
Imran Khan’s transfer follows months of health concerns, including a dispute over worsening vision in his right eye

Imprisoned former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan was shifted from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination, news agency AP reported citing Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party's statement.Khan was taken to Shifa International Hospital hours after Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government would comply with a Supreme Court order directing authorities to facilitate his medical examination.The PTI said the transfer was carried out following the Supreme Court's order earlier this week but did not provide further details. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there.Earlier Thursday, Chaudhry said the government had approached the Supreme Court seeking clarification on whether the medical relief granted to Khan applied only to him or could also cover other prisoners. He stressed that the request was not aimed at delaying or defying the court's order.The three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination amid prolonged concerns raised by his family and personal doctors over his health and access to treatment.The court directed that a medical board examine him, including specialists and his personal physician, Faisal Sultan.The government has maintained that prisoners receive medical care under existing rules and can be moved to government hospitals when required.Concerns over Khan's health intensified in January after his family claimed he had lost about 85% of the vision in his right eye. The government disputed the claim and later said his vision had improved by around 70%.Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. He has remained imprisoned since 2023 after convictions in multiple cases, including a graft case.
Article Summary: Imran Khan was moved from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there. Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no- confidence vote in April 2022.

Article Title: Red-faced Pakistan summons top diplomat over US envoy Gor's J&K remark in Srinagar
Article Text:
US Ambassador Sergio Gor visits Srinagar with J&K CM Omar

Pakistan on Wednesday summoned the top US diplomat Islamabad and lodged a protest after US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India” during his visit to Srinagar on Wednesday.The remarks came as Gor made his first visit to Jammu and Kashmir since taking office and met chief minister Omar Abdullah.Gor’s comments were made during a joint media briefing with Abdullah following their meeting at the chief minister’s residence. “It’s a pleasure to be here. This is an important part of India. I am here, visiting for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place. I am thrilled to be here,” the US envoy said.Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for Jammu and Kashmir, saying the US regularly reviews its warnings. He said the Indian government and the Jammu and Kashmir administration had taken steps to improve safety in the region.“I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at,” Gor said, adding that the US would consider whether its existing travel warning should be downgraded.The ambassador also described his meeting with Abdullah as “very good” and said the two sides had discussed ways to deepen economic cooperation and create opportunities benefiting India and the US.Abdullah said the talks focused on what Washington could do for Jammu and Kashmir, while also referring to “certain legacy issues” that would need to be addressed.“We look forward to taking this conversation further,” Abdullah said, adding that he was “very hopeful and optimistic” that engagement between the US and Jammu and Kashmir would “both widen and deepen in the years ahead”.
Article Summary: Pakistan summons top US diplomat Islamabad and lodges a protest. US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India’ Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for J&K.

Article Title: Nepal floods: No contact with 285 Indians in Nepal, another 200 stranded on China side - key points
Article Text:
Search on for missing people as Nepal flood toll rises

285 Indians remain unaccountable: MEA

Jaishankar reviews flood situation

India sends second relief consignment

Hundreds killed, more than 1,300 missing

Glacier collapse behind deadly floods

Nepal is battling the aftermath of catastrophic floods and landslides triggered by a glacier collapse, with hundreds killed and more than 1,300 people reported missing across Nepal and Tibet. Rescue teams are racing against difficult terrain, damaged roads and bridges, and the risk of further disasters as relief operations continue in the Himalayan region.India has intensified efforts to trace its nationals affected by the disaster, with external affairs minister S Jaishankar reviewing the situation with senior MEA officials and Indian ambassadors in Kathmandu and Beijing. The MEA is coordinating with Nepalese authorities, state governments, tour operators and project agencies to establish the status and well-being of Indians in the affected areas.Two hundred and eighty-five Indian nationals remain unaccounted for following the devastating flash floods in Nepal, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the missing Indians included people working on hydropower projects as well as members of tourist groups. Of the 288, 73 are employees of the Trishuli One Power Project, with the Indian embassy in Kathmandu in touch with the project's head to gather more information.Jaiswal also said 21 Indians from Tamil Nadu had been rescued following the floods, while around 200 Indians in Tibet had sought assistance from India.“India is standing shoulder-to-shoulder with Nepal in this difficult time and we are ready to provide all assistance as per requirements of that country,” he added.Jaishankar held a review meeting with foreign secretary Vikram Misri, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal and other officials, as well as India's ambassadors in Kathmandu and Beijing."Held a review meeting with foreign secretary, Team MEA and our ambassadors in Kathmandu & Beijing on the Nepal flood disaster. Urgent efforts are underway to ascertain the status and well-being of all Indians in the flood-affected areas," Jaishankar said in a post on X/"MEA is coordinating with various ministries, state governments, tour operators and project authorities in this regard. We are working closely with the Nepali side, both on this aspect and on the relief efforts," he added.India has dispatched a second tranche of humanitarian assistance to Nepal. Jaishankar said a flight carrying 37.5 tonnes of humanitarian assistance and disaster relief material, medicines and food packets had departed for Nepal.This followed an initial 10-tonne consignment of relief material, including essential medicines, sent on Wednesday. Indian ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava handed over the supplies to Nepal's minister for culture, tourism and civil aviation Khadak Raj Paudel in Kathmandu.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also spoken with Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Wednesday and offered India's support for rescue and relief operations.The disaster has killed at least 332 people in Nepal and left 826 missing, while three people have died and 558 remain missing in Tibet, according to authorities cited in reports.Nepal's army has rescued more than 100 people through helicopter operations, while at least eight foreign nationals were airlifted to Kathmandu. Dozens of bridges and nearly 40 km of roads were damaged, complicating rescue operations.Helpline numbers have been initiated to help those in need.The US geological survey later determined that the event initially reported as an earthquake was a magnitude 5.2 glacier collapse that sent a destructive torrent downstream.Experts at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said an avalanche from a glacier likely triggered the flash flood. Water levels in the Trishuli river rose by as much as 9 metres within half an hour, underscoring the speed and scale of the disaster.
Article Summary: Two hundred and eighty-five Indian nationals remain unaccounted for following the devastating flash floods in Nepal. The disaster has killed at least 332 people in Nepal and left 826 missing, while three people have died and 558 remain missing in Tibet. Rescue teams are racing against difficult terrain, damaged roads and bridges, and the risk of further disasters.

Article Title: 'OMG, OMG!' Villagers run for life as flash flood chases them after swallowing bridge - watch video
Article Text:
People running away for safety as from huge wave

Roads, bridges swept away

India, UN offer help

A flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa district sent torrents of muddy water and debris through communities along the Nepal-China border, with terrifying videos capturing people scrambling for safety as the waters surged through the region. At least 162 people have been killed and hundreds remain missing after the disaster.One video, filmed by a construction worker in Mailung, shows a sudden torrent sweeping into a work area as the entire crew scrambles to escape the rushing water and debris. The workers can be seen running for safety as the flood rapidly engulfs the site.A separate CCTV video from the Gyirong Port immigration office in Tibet, near the Nepal-China border, captures the destructive force of the flood. A massive wave of mud and silt surges past the building's windows, overwhelming surrounding infrastructure within seconds as people flee the area.Nepal police reported at least 157 deaths, while China's state broadcaster CCTV said three people were killed and 265 remained missing in Tibet's Gyirong County.The disaster has also left hundreds of foreign nationals unaccounted for. Nepalese authorities said 403 people, including 341 foreigners, were reported missing, among them 133 Indians travelling towards Mount Kailash.At least 47 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons and 24 Canadians were also reported missing.The Nepal Tourism Board said 62 Nepali citizens were among those missing after trekking in the Gosaikunda Lake area of Rasuwa. At least 28 police personnel were also reported missing.The disaster was initially believed to have been linked to an earthquake after seismic activity was detected near the Nepal-China border. The US Geological Survey later ruled out an earthquake, saying the seismic activity was caused by a magnitude 5.2 glacial collapse.The collapse sent ice, rock and debris downstream, triggering a sudden surge that caused catastrophic damage in the valleys below. Satellite imagery and assessments by climate researchers also pointed to an ice-rock avalanche from a glacier as the likely trigger.Researchers at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said water levels in the Trishuli River rose by as much as 9 metres in just half an hour, highlighting the speed at which the disaster unfolded.The floods struck with little warning through steep valleys that serve as important transport and economic corridors. At least 19 bridges and nearly 40 km of roads were washed away, while the Bhotekoshi River surged through communities, damaging villages and hydropower infrastructure.The destruction has complicated rescue operations, with damaged roads and bridges cutting off affected areas. Nepal has sought assistance from India and China as authorities continue searching for survivors and those still missing.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered India's assistance with rescue and relief operations.“India is prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance,” Modi said, adding that Indian teams were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.UN agencies are also deploying personnel to support the response, with UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warning of a “massive humanitarian need.”The disaster has renewed concerns about the vulnerability of the Himalayan region to extreme weather and glacial hazards.A similar flash flood struck the region last August after a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed amid high temperatures, killing nine people and damaging key infrastructure, including a bridge linking Nepal and China.Scientists have warned that accelerating glacier melt across the Hindu Kush Himalaya is increasing the risk of glacial floods, landslides and sudden water surges, making early-warning systems increasingly critical in a warming mountain region.
Article Summary: Flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa district kills 162 and leaves hundreds missing. Terrifying videos capture people scrambling for safety as waters surge through the region. At least 19 bridges and nearly 40 km of roads were washed away, while the Bhotekoshi River surged through communities.

Article Title: Nepal: Video captures moment raging flash flood engulfs entire village
Article Text:
Entire village engulfed by raging flash flood in terrifying video (Video credit: X)

Footage filmed by locals captures the terrifying moment a massive flash flood tears through a village in Nepal, sending residents running for higher ground as torrents of mud and water sweep through the settlement.In one of the videos, people can be seen fleeing as floodwaters surge through the area, while others scramble towards higher ground to escape the rapidly rising water. Another video shows a bridge collapsing under the force of the torrent as people watch from nearby.The flood swept away homes, vehicles and other infrastructure within seconds, leaving large parts of the affected area covered in mud and debris. Buses and cars were seen being engulfed by the floodwaters as the torrent moved through the village.The footage comes as rescue teams search for hundreds of people still missing after a wall of mud and rock collapsed into a river along the Nepal-China border on Wednesday, triggering catastrophic flooding across Himalayan valleys.Nepal Police said 157 bodies had been recovered, while officials said more than 400 tourists were missing, including around 340 foreigners. Many of those missing were travelling through the region on pilgrimage or trekking trips.The US Geological Survey later said seismic activity recorded during the disaster was caused by glacial rock and ice collapsing and the subsequent movement of debris, rather than a separate earthquake.An initial study of satellite imagery indicated that an ice-and-rock landslide triggered a debris-laden flood in the Lhende River, about 20 kilometres northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border crossing.The disaster washed away houses, roads and power infrastructure, while a metal bridge was also seen being swept away by the floodwaters."There is devastation everywhere we look," Tula Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa, told Reuters. "The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing."Rescue operations have been hampered by damaged roads, disrupted communications and difficult weather. Helicopters were unable to land in some of the worst-hit areas, including Syapru Besi and Timure in Rasuwa district.
Article Summary: Footage shows entire village engulfed by raging flash flood in Nepal. Flood swept away homes, vehicles and other infrastructure within seconds. Comes as rescue teams search for hundreds of people still missing after disaster. A wall of mud and rock collapsed into a river along the Nepal-China border.

Trail of devastation caused by floods

Nepal came under the sudden force of a massive flood on Wednesday, leaving a trail of devastation as the Himalayan fury claimed at least 165 lives and left more than 1300 people missing.The Himalayan nation’s northern region bore the brunt of the disaster, with Rasuwa district on China-Nepal border among the worst-hit areas.The fury was carried by the Bhote Koshi River, which originates in Tibet and came rushing down with enormous force, carrying with it ice, rocks, mud and debris.The aftermath offers a stark picture of the destruction left behind. Floods, landslides, avalanches and droughts are becoming more frequent and severe across the region, while rapid changes to water, land and air are posing a major threat to millions of people, according to the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD).The organisation said on Wednesday that the flash flood sent a powerful surge of water, sediment and boulders through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems.In the downstream Galchhi area, water levels in the river reportedly rose by as much as nine metres, nearly 30 feet, in just 30 minutes.

Article Title: Before and after: Satellite images show how Nepal’s green mountainside turned into debris field
Article Text:
A combination of satellite images shows the valleys near the Nepal-China border on August 23, 2026, before the devastating floods and on August 26, 2026, after the disaster. (Photo: Reuters)

Satellite pictures point to the starting point

A satellite image shows Manakamana before a flash flood affected the area, Nepal, August 23, 2026. (Photo: Reuters)

A satellite image shows the valleys near the Nepal-China border on August 26, 2026, after the devastating floods. (Photo: Reuters)

Snow cover changed sharply before disaster

Seismic signal traced to the collapse

Search for hundreds still missing

Surge sent water levels soaring

India evacuates thousands, offers Nepal assistance

A drove view of mud covered properties following a flash flood at Trishuli in Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 26, 2026. (Photo: Reuters)

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most pressing issue faced by communities affected by the flood? Search and rescue operations Restoration of infrastructure Providing humanitarian aid 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Satellite images taken before and after the deadly flash flood near Nepal’s border with Tibet reveal a striking change in the landscape: stretches of green mountainside visible before the disaster are now covered by a broad expanse of brown debris and sediment.The Planet Labs imagery has provided early clues to how the disaster may have started. Experts examining the pictures believe that the lower section of a glacier broke away high in the mountains and plunged hundreds of metres into the valley below, likely carrying or entraining rock and sediment as it fell.Early reports raised an earthquake as a possible trigger, but the US Geological Survey later said the recorded seismic activity came from the collapse itself rather than a separate earthquake, according to news agency Reuters.Sikkim University academic Vikram Gupta, an engineering geology specialist, said the satellite evidence indicated that the collapse began at the glacier’s lower end."It’s confirmed that a substantial portion of that glacier snout collapsed to initiate the event - probably including or entraining a fair amount of rock and sediment," Gupta said.Dan Shugar, an earth scientist and associate professor at the University of Calgary, also traced the apparent origin of the disaster to a glacier high above the valley."What I can see in this morning's satellite imagery from Planet Labs, the lower part of a glacier broke off at about 5,200 metres and crashed onto the valley floor about 1,200 metres below," Shugar said.The resulting ice-rock avalanche sent a destructive surge downstream, eventually carrying water, sediment and boulders through the river systems below.A Planet Labs pair taken a day apart captures the border valleys on August 25 and August 26, effectively bracketing the disaster. Other comparisons track the transformation of Manakamana and Khadga Bhanjyang between August 23 and August 26.Floodwaters surged through communities along the Bhote Koshi. Rasuwa and nearby districts suffered widespread damage, including to transport links, homes and power infrastructure.The satellite imagery also showed another significant change in the mountains in the hours before the flood.Comparing satellite images taken roughly a day apart, Shugar noticed a pronounced loss of snow cover."Some of the glaciers in the valley were covered in snow yesterday and today they are mostly bare ice. So in other words (and I haven't seen any weather station data yet), it was probably warm," he said.Whether those warmer conditions contributed directly to the collapse has not yet been established.Nepal’s glaciers have already been undergoing significant long-term changes. A 2023 United Nations assessment found that Nepal’s snow-covered mountains had lost nearly a third of their ice over a little more than three decades because of global warming.It also found that Nepal's glaciers melted 65% faster over the preceding decade than during the decade before it.An initial assessment by Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority indicated that an ice-and-rock landslide triggered the debris-laden flood in the Lhende River, around 20 kilometres northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border crossing.Prakash Pokharel, a geologist with the authority who reviewed the Planet Labs images, identified the immediate event as an avalanche involving both ice and rock."The flash floods were caused by an ice-rock avalanche on the Nepali side," Pokharel said.The USGS assessment provided further clarity on the early earthquake theory. What had initially been identified as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake was subsequently determined to be seismic activity produced by the collapse of glacial rock and ice and the movement of debris, rather than a separate quake preceding the disaster.Shugar said construction activity could also be a factor. On the broader question of global warming, he said "whether climate change played a role is something we will no doubt be looking into in the near future".Search teams have struggled to reach parts of the disaster zone, where poor weather and communications failures have complicated efforts to locate survivors and assess the damage. Rescue helicopters were also unable to land in Syapru Besi and Timure as conditions and disrupted access hampered operations.Rasuwa, a mountainous district of roughly 50,000 people, is also home to several hydropower projects in areas hit hardest by the disaster.By late Wednesday, police in Nepal had recovered 157 bodies. More than 400 tourists were still unaccounted for in Nepal, with tourism officials saying around 340 were foreigners.Many of those caught in the disaster were travelling through the region on pilgrimages to Kailash Mansarovar.Across the border in Tibet, Chinese state media reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Gyirong, while cautioning that the toll was still being verified. The mudslide also severed road, communications and power connections in the border area.According to the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development, floodwaters swept sediment and boulders into both the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems as the surge travelled downstream.At Galchhi, the river reportedly climbed roughly nine metres — about 30 feet — in half an hour.Downstream concerns also reached India. Disaster-response units were put on alert in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh as officials watched for the flood surge from Nepal to enter the Gandak river system.An earlier Central Water Commission advisory, issued after a sudden rise in the Trishuli at Furke Khola, about 160 kilometres from India, had raised the possibility of glacial lake outburst flood activity near the Nepal-China border.Districts along the Gandak's downstream course in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh were told to maintain heightened surveillance.About 5,000 residents had already been moved to safety from six Bihar districts by Thursday, with preparations covering as many as 10,000 to 12,000 people if further evacuations were required.Prime Minister Narendra Modi conveyed condolences to Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered humanitarian assistance, saying Indian teams were working with Nepalese authorities on rescue and relief.The disaster also comes against a backdrop of more frequent and increasingly powerful extreme events across the Hindu Kush Himalayas, including floods, landslides, avalanches and droughts.For now, the satellite record is helping investigators reconstruct how the catastrophe unfolded — from the apparent collapse of ice and rock high in the mountains to the destructive torrent that swept through valleys, settlements and river systems far downstream.
Article Summary: Satellite images taken before and after the deadly flash flood near Nepal’s border with Tibet reveal a striking change in the landscape. Experts believe that the lower section of a glacier broke away high in the mountains and plunged hundreds of metres into the valley below. The resulting ice-rock avalanche sent a destructive surge downstream, eventually carrying water, sediment and boulders through the river systems below.
